headline: Users of Chinese AI companion chatbots are grieving after new rules led ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen to scrap the feature.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: the rules date from July, but this is new first-hand reporting and the 15 Oct 2026 deletion date is three days away; it rests on a few users, not a survey.
importance_line: What changed is that regulation is cutting people's emotional ties to chatbots, which affects users of companion chatbots first, then platforms such as ByteDance and Alibaba, then regulators weighing addiction against grief, but the report rests on a handful of users and researchers and gives no count of those affected.
summary: Sixth Tone reports that users in China are grieving the loss of their AI companions, customised chatbots often modelled on game characters or former partners, after rules in force since 15 Jul 2026 banned services that "induce emotional dependence or harm real-life relationships" and ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen scrapped the feature. Doubao users have until 15 Oct 2026, when characters are permanently deleted, to move them to its sister app Maoxiang, and a Tsinghua University professor quoted warns that AI romance can breed addiction and loneliness.
notes: Full text read. Underlying rules and shutdowns date from 15 Jul 2026; the feature adds first-hand accounts and the 15 Oct 2026 deletion date.
